51541-louise-imogen-guiney.title: Louise Imogen Guiney
51541-louise-imogen-guiney.creator: Alice Brown
51541-louise-imogen-guiney.description: A book by Alice Brown. There was between them that “marriage of true minds” which is more lastingly productive than the tie of blood, and she was proud if you could trace in her the reflex of those qualities she held highest in him: his active patriotism, his slack hold on life, if it could be nobly given, and a tenacity of devotion to the brave fight.

arxiv-2007-10163.title: Bayesian Non-Parametric Detection Heterogeneity in Ecological Models
arxiv-2007-10163.creator: D. Turek ∗ Williams College, Williamstown, USA, C. Wehrhahn ∗ University of California, Santa Cruz, USA, O. Gimenez ∗ CNRS, France
arxiv-2007-10163.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by D. Turek ∗ Williams College, Williamstown, USA, C. Wehrhahn ∗ University of California, Santa Cruz, USA, O. Gimenez ∗ CNRS, France. Detection heterogeneity is inherent to ecological data, arising from factors such as varied terrain or weather conditions, inconsistent sampling effort, or heterogeneity of individuals themselves.

arxiv-2110-11446.creator: Şeyma Selcan Mağara, Ceren Yıldırım, Ferhat Yaman, Berke Dilekoğlu, Furkan Reha Tutaş, Erdinç Öztürk, Kamer Kaya, Öznur Taştan, Erkay Savaş
arxiv-2110-11446.description: Abstract . Preserving the privacy and security of big data in the context of cloud computing, while maintaining a certain level of efficiency of its processing remains to be a subject, open for improvement. One of the most popular applications epitomizing said concerns is found to be useful in genome analysis.

arxiv-2206-04402.creator: Taekyun Kim*, DAE SAN KIM*, Hyekyung Kim*
arxiv-2206-04402.description: Abstract . The degenerate Stirling numbers of the second kind and of the first kind, which are respectively degenerate versions of the Stirling numbers of the second kind and of the first kind, appear frequently when we study various degenerate versions of some special numbers and polynomials.

arxiv-2210-12170.title: Discovering Differences in the Representation of People using Contextualized Semantic Axes
arxiv-2210-12170.creator: Li Lucy, Divya Tadimeti, David Bamman
arxiv-2210-12170.description: Abstract A common paradigm for identifying semantic differences across social and temporal contexts is the use of static word embeddings and their distances. In particular, past work has compared embeddings against “semantic axes” that represent two opposing concepts. We extend this paradigm to BERT embeddings, and construct contextualized axes that mitigate the pitfall where antonyms have neighboring representations.

arxiv-2310-10946.title: Multi-point Feedback of Bandit Convex Optimization with Hard Constraints
arxiv-2310-10946.creator: Yasunari Hikima
arxiv-2310-10946.description: Abstract This paper studies bandit convex optimization with constraints, where the learner aims to generate a sequence of decisions under partial information of loss functions such that the cumulative loss is reduced as well as the cumulative constraint violation is simultaneously reduced.

arxiv-2411-01371.title: Network Causal Effect Estimation In Graphical Models Of Contagion And Latent Confounding
arxiv-2411-01371.creator: Yufeng Wu, Rohit Bhattacharya
arxiv-2411-01371.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yufeng Wu, Rohit Bhattacharya. A key question in many network studies is whether the observed correlations between units are primarily due to contagion or latent confounding. Here, we study this question using a segregated graph ( Shpitser, 2015 ) representation of these mechanisms, and examine how uncertainty about the true underlying mechanism impacts downstream computation of network causal effects, particularly under full interference—settings where we only have a single realization of a network and each unit may depend on any other unit in the

arxiv-2506-00593.title: Look mom, no experimental data! Learning to score protein-ligand interactions from simulations
arxiv-2506-00593.creator: Michael BrocidiaconoJames WellnitzKonstantin I. PopovAlexander TropshaEshelman School of PharmacyUniversity of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
arxiv-2506-00593.description: Abstract Despite recent advances in protein-ligand structure prediction, deep learning methods remain limited in their ability to accurately predict binding affinities, particularly for novel protein targets dissimilar from the training set. In contrast, physics-based binding free energy calculations offer high accuracy across chemical space but are computationally prohibitive for large-scale screening.

arxiv-2506-20652.title: EditP23: 3D Editing via Propagation of Image Prompts to Multi-View Journal: TOG 1862
arxiv-2506-20652.creator: Roi Bar-On, Dana Cohen-Bar, Daniel Cohen-Or
arxiv-2506-20652.description: Abstract . We present EditP23, a method for mask-free 3D editing that propagates 2D image edits to multi-view representations in a 3D-consistent manner. In contrast to traditional approaches that rely on text-based prompting or explicit spatial masks, EditP23 enables intuitive edits by conditioning on a pair of images: an original view and its user-edited counterpart.

arxiv-2506-22144.title: Wait-Only Broadcast Protocols are Easier to Verify
arxiv-2506-22144.creator: Lucie Guillou, Arnaud Sangnier, Nathalie Sznajder
arxiv-2506-22144.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lucie Guillou, Arnaud Sangnier, Nathalie Sznajder. We study networks of processes that all execute the same finite-state protocol and communicate via broadcasts. We are interested in two problems with a parameterized number of processes: the synchronization problem which asks whether there is an execution which puts all processes on a given state; and the repeated coverability problem which asks if there is an infinite execution where a given transition is taken infinitely often.

arxiv-2510-06932.title: Homotopy theory of simplicial parametrized operads
arxiv-2510-06932.creator: Grégoire Marc
arxiv-2510-06932.description: Abstract Abstract We define a generalization of (coloured) operads based on double lax functors and we construct a model structure on the associated category of generalized simplicial (coloured) operads. In particular, we obtain a model structure on the category of simplicial (coloured) {\mathscr{O}} -operads of Nardin and Shah. 1.

pmc-10495398.title: Near index matching enables solid diffractive optical element fabrication via additive manufacturing
pmc-10495398.creator: Reut Orange kedem, Nadav Opatovski, Dafei Xiao, Boris Ferdman, Onit Alalouf, Sushanta Kumar Pal, Ziyun Wang, Henrik von der Emde, Michael Weber, Steffen J. Sahl, Aleks Ponjavic, Ady Arie, Stefan W. Hell, Yoav Shechtman
pmc-10495398.description: Diffractive optical elements (DOEs) have a wide range of applications in optics and photonics, thanks to their capability to perform complex wavefront shaping in a compact form. However, widespread applicability of DOEs is still limited, because existing fabrication methods are cumbersome and expensive. Here, we present a simple and cost-effective fabrication approach for solid, high-performance DOEs.

pmc-11334566.title: Efficacy of NKG2D CAR-T cells with IL-15/IL-15Rα signaling for treating Epstein-Barr virus-associated lymphoproliferative disorder
pmc-11334566.creator: Qiusui Mai, Bailin He, Shikai Deng, Qing Zeng, Yanwen Xu, Cong Wang, Yunyi Pang, Sheng Zhang, Jinfeng Li, Jinfeng Zeng, Liqin Huang, Yongshui Fu, Chengyao Li, Tingting Li, Xiaojun Xu, Ling Zhang
pmc-11334566.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) related post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (EBV-PTLD) is a life-threatening complication after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) or solid organ transplantation (SOT), for which no standard therapeutic means have been developed. Significant increase expression of natural killer group 2 member D ligands (NKG2DLs) was observed on B-lymphoblastoid cells of EBV-PTLD, indicating NKG2DLs as potential therapeutic targets for treatment of EBV-PTLD.

pmc-11454275.title: 8656 A Case of Wolfram Syndrome Accompanied by Growth Hormone Deficiency
pmc-11454275.creator: Hyeon Jun Jung, Goo Lyeon Kim, Yooyeon Park, Jeesuk Yu
pmc-11454275.description: Disclosure: H. Jung: None. G. Kim: None. Y. Park: None. J. Yu: None. Background: This case report explores the presentation, diagnosis, and multidisciplinary management of an 11-year-old female patient with Wolfram syndrome, a rare and progressive genetic disorder. Wolfram syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterized by early-onset diabetes mellitus, diabetes insipidus, optic nerve atrophy, hearing loss, and neurodegeneration.

pmc-11464940.title: Ascertaining Out-of-Pocket Costs of Dementia Care: Feasibility Study of a Web-Based Weekly Survey
pmc-11464940.creator: Walter D Dawson, Nora Mattek, Sarah Gothard, Jeffrey Kaye, Allison Lindauer
pmc-11464940.description: BackgroundCaring for a family member living with dementia is costly. A major contributor to care demands, and therefore to the costs, are the behavioral symptoms of dementia. Here, we examine the feasibility of ascertaining costs related to caregiving from weekly web-based surveys collected during a telehealth-based behavioral intervention study—Support via Technology: Living and Learning with Advancing Alzheimer Disease.

pmc-11503724.title: Insights into the Gut Microbial Diversity of Wild Siberian Musk Deer (Moschus moschiferus) in Republic of Korea
pmc-11503724.creator: Nari Kim, Kyung-Hyo Do, Chea-Un Cho, Kwang-Won Seo, Dong-Hyuk Jeong
pmc-11503724.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThe Siberian musk deer is a vulnerable species, and understanding its health is crucial for conservation. This study investigated the gut microbiome of wild Siberian musk deer in three different locations in Republic of Korea. By analyzing fecal samples through 16S rRNA sequencing, we observed significant differences in the alpha diversity among Siberian musk deer from various habitats, while the beta diversity showed no significant differences.

pmc-11714032.title: Supporting Participants in Preclinical Alzheimer’s Trials: Experience from a Research Participant Advisory Board and the A4 Study
pmc-11714032.creator: Sarah Walter, Guadalupe Morales, Elizabeth Shaffer‐Bacareza, Jason Karlawish, Joshua D Grill, Michael C Donohue, Paula Cohen, Paul S S Aisen, Reisa A Sperling, The A4 Study Team
pmc-11714032.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Preclinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD) trials can involve multiple years of follow‐up and burdensome procedures for older individuals. Optimizing the design and conduct of these trials requires input from participants and their families. Since 2020, the Alzheimer’s Clinical Trials Consortium (ACTC) Research Participant Advisory Board has provided input on study attributes including: participant and study partner compensation, consent language, and result communication tools. A key recommendation from the advisory board is to design studies with the option to learn individual research results.

pmc-11970483.title: Metabolomic Approach in Anticancer Biomarker Discovery from Foliose Lichens
pmc-11970483.creator: Chintya Permata Zahky Sukrisno Putri, Dinar Mutia Rani, Ludmilla Fitri Untari, Banun Kusumawardani, Anang Kurnia, Paul A. Keller, Ari Satia Nugraha
pmc-11970483.description: Purpose: Lichens are well-known as a source of pharmacologically active compounds. This includes anticancer compounds which have biomass constraints including using traditional techniques of lichen bioprospecting. This current study reports the use of cutting-edge metabolomics and a computational approach to discover anticancer biomarkers from Indonesian lichens.

pmc-12420349.title: Economic Burden of Diseases Caused by Air Pollution in Iran: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-12420349.creator: Nikta Shobeiri, Amin Adel, Asma Rashki Kemmak
pmc-12420349.description: Background and AimsAir pollution refers to the presence of one or more pollutants or compounds in outdoor or indoor air in concentrations and durations that can harm human health, plants, animals, or possessions, or lead to undue disruption of a person's ability to enjoy their life or belongings comfortably.

pmc-12653712.title: Rehabilitation Intervention for an Infant with Simple Epidermolysis Bullosa from NICU to Home Discharge: A Case Report
pmc-12653712.creator: Tetsuo Sakai, Syoichi Tashiro, Aki Karasuyama, Toshihiko Kimura, Masami Narita, Shin Yamada
pmc-12653712.description: Background/Objectives: Reports detailing rehabilitative interventions for infants with severe dermatologic disorders are scarce. Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) is a genetic disorder characterized by skin fragility, which causes blistering after minor trauma. Since there is still no cure in general clinics, symptomatic treatment and developmental support are essential for managing the condition.

pmc-13218240.title: Provoking disulfidptosis-enhanced mitophagy by manganese-based nanoplatform via regulating cellular energy supply and redox homeostasis
pmc-13218240.creator: Zhenying Diao, Bin Feng, Yanfei Fu, Youcheng Liang, Long Qiu, Jianbo Sun, Yanlei Liu, Daxiang Cui, Ting Yin
pmc-13218240.description: Metabolic reprogramming and reinforcing redox defense mechanisms in tumors remains major obstacles to oxidative stress therapies in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). To address these obstacles, we strategically targeted cystine transporter SLC7A11, which plays a central role in cellular redox homeostasis.
